entry.title: E-2026-008 Texas and North Carolina Senate: ballot counts were too high
entry.summary: Corrected. Our notes said 7 candidates were on the Texas Senate ballot and 5 in North Carolina. Both counts came from Ballotpedia. The Texas Secretary of State lists 3 on the ballot (Paxton, Talarico and Brown); the other 4 names were certified write-ins. The North Carolina State Board of Elections lists 4 (Cooper, Whatley, Bray and Dublin); two names in our count were not on its list.

entry.title: E-2026-007 Wisconsin governor: the ballot count was too high
entry.summary: Corrected. Our note said 3 candidates were on the Wisconsin governor ballot. That count came from Ballotpedia and included a registered write-in. The Wisconsin Elections Commission's Candidates on Ballot list shows 2: Tiffany (Republican) and Crowley (Democratic). Both are on our map, so the map is complete.

entry.title: E-2026-006 Nebraska Senate: ballot count corrected again, from three to five
entry.summary: Corrected. E-2026-004 said three candidates were on the ballot. Five were: Ricketts, Osborn, Robin Richards, Mike Marvin and Chuck Conboy. Marvin suspended his campaign but stayed on the ballot. The Nebraska Examiner and The Green Papers both report five.

entry.title: E-2026-005 Georgia and South Carolina Senate: ballot counts were too high
entry.summary: Corrected. Our notes said 7 candidates were on the ballot in Georgia and 10 in South Carolina. Both counts came from Ballotpedia and included people who were not on the general election ballot. The Green Papers lists 2 for Georgia (Ossoff and Collins, plus 3 write-ins) and 4 for South Carolina (Andrews, Graham, Whitener and Hackett). The South Carolina vote shares add up to 100% across those four plus write-ins, so no other name was on the ballot. Georgia is now complete on our map.

entry.title: E-2026-004 Nebraska Senate: ballot count corrected from five to three
entry.summary: Corrected. Our note and card said two of five candidates were on the ballot. A July Ballotpedia report listed three on the ballot after the Democratic nominee withdrew. A later Ballotpedia headline counts five names.

entry.title: E-2026-003 The "Votes cast" bar counted only the two shown candidates
entry.summary: Corrected. The bar labelled "Votes cast" used the sum of the two shown candidates' votes as its total, so it read as a share of all votes cast. On 53 pages that is not what it measures.

entry.title: E-2026-002 Thirty-seven more pages map only some of the candidates on the ballot
entry.summary: Open. According to The Green Papers or Ballotpedia, these pages show two candidates while more were on the ballot. Senate: AR, CO, FL, IA, ID, IL, KY, MI, MN, MS, NC, NE, NJ, OK, OR, SC, TN, TX. Governor: WY, AR, AZ, CO, FL, ID, IL, MI, MN, NE, NV, OH, OK, OR, PA, SC, TN, WI. House: ND. Shares on these pages are shares of the two shown candidates, not of all votes. California (top-two), Alabama, Georgia, Kansas, New Mexico, New York (including the two New York City pages), Louisiana, Iowa governor, Wyoming Senate and the South Dakota races are complete. All 54 pages have now been checked.

entry.title: E-2026-001 Montana Senate map shows two of the candidates on the ballot
entry.summary: Disclosed on page. The page maps Seth Bodnar (independent) and Kurt Alme (Republican) only. It leaves out Democrat Alani Bankhead, Libertarian Kyle Austin and one write-in candidate. The headline share is therefore a share of the two shown candidates' votes, not of all votes.
